subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which prominent minority leader served as India's first Minister of Education in the Union Cabinet headed by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, a distinguished scholar and freedom fighter, served as India's first Education Minister from 1947 until his death in 1958.

questions.question: In which year were the Portuguese-ruled territories of Goa, Daman, and Diu liberated and integrated into India through military operation 'Operation Vijay'?
questions.explanation: The Indian armed forces launched Operation Vijay on 18-19 December 1961, bringing over four centuries of Portuguese colonial rule in Goa, Daman, and Diu to an end.

questions.question: Which visionary Gandhian reformer launched the historic Bhoodan (Land Gift) movement in Pochampally village in April 1951?
questions.explanation: Acharya Vinoba Bhave initiated the voluntary land-donation movement known as Bhoodan at Pochampally (now Telangana) on 18 April 1951.

questions.question: Following the 1971 war, the 1949 UN Ceasefire Line in Jammu and Kashmir was designated as what in the Shimla Agreement?
questions.explanation: Under the Shimla Agreement of July 1972, both nations agreed that the ceasefire line resulting from the 1971 war would henceforth be respected as the Line of Control (LoC).

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which veteran political leader from Andhra Pradesh was chosen as the official Congress candidate for the presidency of India in 1969 by the Syndicate?
questions.explanation: The Syndicate nominated Lok Sabha Speaker Neelam Sanjiva Reddy as the official party candidate for the 1969 presidential contest against Indira Gandhi's wishes.

questions.question: Who was the younger son of Indira Gandhi who wielded enormous extra-constitutional authority during the Emergency, spearheading family planning and slum clearance drives?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Gandhi exercised pervasive informal political authority during the Emergency, directing the 5-point program including aggressive demographic control and urban demolitions.

questions.question: The catastrophic bamboo flowering famine of 1959, known locally as 'Mautam', occurred in which hill district, sparking regional discontent against the state of Assam?
questions.explanation: The 1959 Mautam famine in the Mizo Hills district and the perceived apathy of the Assam state administration led to the formation of the Mizo National Famine Front, later the MNF.

questions.question: On 21 May 1991, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi was tragically assassinated by an LTTE suicide bomber at an election rally in:
questions.explanation: Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by an LTTE suicide bomber (Dhanu) on 21 May 1991 while campaigning at Sriperumbudur, near Chennai, Tamil Nadu.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In 1989, Soviet troops completely withdrew from which neighboring country after a decade-long military intervention that severely drained Soviet finances?
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev ordered the complete withdrawal of the Soviet 40th Army from Afghanistan, which was completed in February 1989.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: In which Chinese coastal fishing town did Deng Xiaoping establish China's very first Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in 1980?
questions.explanation: Shenzhen, adjacent to Hong Kong, was designated as China's first Special Economic Zone in 1980, transforming from a small fishing town into a mega-industrial metropolis.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which Himalayan kingdom adopted the distinctive holistic developmental metric of 'Gross National Happiness' (GNH) under its monarchy?
questions.explanation: Bhutan's 4th King, Jigme Singye Wangchuck, enunciated 'Gross National Happiness' (GNH) in 1972, prioritizing environmental conservation, spiritual well-being, and cultural preservation over mere GDP.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Where is the global headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) situated?
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO), established on 7 April 1948 as the specialized UN agency for international public health, is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: In the First General Election of 1952, what percentage of the total popular vote did the Indian National Congress win to capture nearly 74% of the Lok Sabha seats?
options: A) Approximately 45% of the total valid votes polled
B) Over 85% of the total valid votes polled
C) Exactly 66% of the total valid votes polled
D) Less than 25% of the total valid votes polled
questions.explanation: Because of India's First-Past-The-Post electoral system, the Congress secured 364 out of 489 seats (74.4%) with only 45% of the popular vote, as opposition votes were fragmented.

questions.question: The Sikh socio-political movement demanding the carving out of a separate Punjabi-speaking state from composite East Punjab was led by which Akali leader?
options: A) Giani Zail Singh and Darbara Singh
B) Master Tara Singh and Sant Fateh Singh
C) Parkash Singh Badal and Surjit Singh Barnala
questions.explanation: Master Tara Singh and later Sant Fateh Singh spearheaded the Punjabi Suba movement from the 1950s, leading to the trifurcation of Punjab into Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal in 1966.

questions.question: Which national institution was set up in 1938 by Congress President Subhas Chandra Bose with Jawaharlal Nehru as Chairman to formulate a blueprint for free India's planned economy?
questions.explanation: In 1938, Subhas Chandra Bose initiated the National Planning Committee with Jawaharlal Nehru as Chairman, bringing together scientists, industrialists, and economists.

questions.question: What role did India play in the settlement of the Korean War (1950-1953) under United Nations auspices?
options: A) India sent two combat armored divisions to reinforce South Korean troops along the 38th parallel
B) India supplied ballistic missiles to North Korea to deter American air strikes
C) India signed a mutual defense treaty with Pyongyang establishing a naval protectorate
D) India served as Chairman of the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission (NNRC) headed by Lieutenant General K.S. Thimayya to supervise the repatriation of prisoners of war
questions.explanation: India served as the neutral mediator in Korea; Lt. Gen. K.S. Thimayya chaired the NNRC, overseeing the delicate custody and repatriation of over 22,000 prisoners of war.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the historic 1969 presidential election, on what basis did independent candidate V.V. Giri secure victory over official Congress candidate Neelam Sanjiva Reddy?
options: A) He won on the count of second-preference votes after no candidate secured the required electoral quota in the first count
B) He secured a unanimous voice vote of all state governors assembled in New Delhi
C) He won automatically because Sanjiva Reddy's nomination papers were rejected by the Election Commission
D) He was declared elected by a special executive ordinance issued by the Acting President
questions.explanation: In the 1969 election, V.V. Giri polled 402,108 value votes in the first round against Reddy's 313,516, and won on the second-preference count after C.D. Deshmukh's votes were transferred.

questions.question: When was the Union Cabinet formally informed about the proclamation of the National Emergency declared on the night of 25 June 1975?
options: A) Three weeks before the proclamation, following a two-day full Cabinet debate in Parliament
B) At a special emergency Cabinet meeting held at 6:00 AM on the morning of 26 June 1975, after the President had already signed the proclamation
C) Concurrently on national television as President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed signed the document
D) Only after the Emergency was officially terminated in March 1977
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi advised the President late on 25 June without prior Cabinet consultation; the Cabinet was informed post-facto at an early morning meeting at 6:00 AM on 26 June.

questions.question: Which of the following was an infamous excess investigated by the Shah Commission in the Turkman Gate area of Old Delhi during the Emergency?
options: A) The total confiscation of all gold jewelry deposited in nationalized banks across Delhi
B) The mandatory conversion of all printing presses into state-owned news agencies
C) Forced eviction of slum dwellers, demolition of residential tenements, and police firing on protesting citizens
D) The nationwide cancellation of all public bus transit services
questions.explanation: The demolition of tenements at Turkman Gate in April 1976 and subsequent police firing on unarmed residents protesting forcible relocation was one of the grimmest excesses exposed by the Shah Commission.

questions.question: What was the primary legal controversy surrounding the Illegal Migrants (Determination by Tribunals) Act, 1983 (IMDT Act) enacted for Assam?
options: A) It mandated the immediate deportation of all Indian citizens residing in the Brahmaputra valley
B) It declared Assam an independent sovereign buffer zone outside the Indian union
C) It abolished all judicial courts across the state of Assam
D) It placed the burden of proof on the complainant and police rather than on the alleged illegal migrant, making deportation virtually impossible
questions.explanation: Unlike the Foreigners Act 1946 where the burden of proving citizenship lies on the individual, the IMDT Act put the burden on the complainant, which the Supreme Court struck down in 2005 as discriminatory.

questions.question: Which political coalition contested the controversial 1987 Jammu and Kashmir Assembly elections against the National Conference-Congress alliance, sparking widespread allegations of electoral rigging?
options: C) Jammu and Kashmir Democratic Freedom Party
questions.explanation: The Muslim United Front (MUF) was a broad coalition of Islamic and regional opposition parties; the widespread rigging of the 1987 elections in favor of the NC-Congress alliance catalyzed armed insurgency.

questions.question: Which political paradox characterized the minority National Front government formed by Prime Minister V.P. Singh in December 1989?
options: A) It held an absolute three-fourths majority in both houses of Parliament without any opposition
B) It was simultaneously supported from the outside by two bitter ideological rivals: the Bharatiya Janata Party (Right) and the Left Front (Communist)
C) It was composed entirely of nominated civil servants with no elected parliamentarians
D) It governed under the direct supervision of the United Nations General Assembly
questions.explanation: The National Front government survived on the external support of both the BJP and the Left Front, who sat on opposite sides of the ideological spectrum and refused to join the ministry.

questions.question: What major step did the P.V. Narasimha Rao government take in July 1991 to dismantle the decades-old 'License Raj' in the industrial sector?
options: A) Nationalising all remaining private sector manufacturing enterprises in India
B) Imposing 500% customs tariffs on all capital equipment imports
C) Abolishing industrial licensing for all but a handful of strategic and hazardous industries under the New Industrial Policy
D) Banning private corporate investments in electronic communications and information technology
questions.explanation: The New Industrial Policy of 24 July 1991 abolished industrial licensing for all projects except 18 specified industries, dismantled MRTP asset limits, and threw open doors to foreign investment.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What was the peaceful, bloodless transition from communist rule to parliamentary democracy in Czechoslovakia in late 1989 called?
questions.explanation: The non-violent transition that ended Communist Party rule in Czechoslovakia between November and December 1989, elevating dissident playwright Vaclav Havel to the presidency, is known as the Velvet Revolution.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which 1997 multilateral economic crisis devastated the currencies and financial systems of Thailand, Indonesia, and South Korea before being stabilized through structural adjustment?
questions.explanation: The Asian Financial Crisis began with the collapse of the Thai baht in July 1997 and rapidly infected Southeast Asian economies and South Korea, prompting massive IMF bailouts.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What is the primary objective of the European Parliament, whose members are directly elected every five years by citizens of all EU member countries?
options: A) Commanding a standing unified continental army of over two million active soldiers
B) Passing EU legislation jointly with the Council of the EU and exercising democratic scrutiny over the European Commission
C) Directly fixing the national income tax rates in every municipality of Western Europe
D) Issuing individual national passports to all citizens born in Europe
questions.explanation: The European Parliament shares legislative and budgetary authority with the Council of the EU and exercises democratic oversight over EU institutions like the European Commission.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: What horrific anti-Tamil pogrom in Sri Lanka in July 1983 is universally regarded as the catalyst that transformed Tamil grievances into full-scale civil warfare?
questions.explanation: The 'Black July' pogrom of July 1983, in which hundreds of Tamils were slaughtered and property destroyed with state complicity following an LTTE ambush, triggered the mass militarization of Tamil youth.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In Pakistan, which military dictator executed elected Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in April 1979 and launched the extensive 'Islamization' of laws and society?
questions.explanation: General Zia-ul-Haq overthrew Bhutto in a coup in 1977, hanged him in 1979 following a contentious judicial trial, and governed Pakistan under strict martial law and Islamization until 1988.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: How are decisions taken in the United Nations General Assembly on 'important questions' such as peace and security, admission of new members, and budgetary matters?
options: A) By a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting
B) By a simple majority where each member has one vote
C) Only with the unanimous concurrence of the five permanent UNSC members
D) By a secret ballot conducted exclusively by the International Court of Justice
questions.explanation: Under Article 18 of the UN Charter, decisions on important questions require a two-thirds majority of members present and voting; other questions require a simple majority.

questions.question: What is the primary rationale behind nuclear-armed states maintaining 'Confidence Building Measures' (CBMs)?
options: A) To coordinate joint offensive invasions against non-nuclear neighboring states
B) To avoid accidental escalation to war by institutionalizing communication, military transparency, and advance notice of troop movements or missile tests
C) To fix the international market export prices for enriched weapons-grade plutonium
D) To transfer sovereign command of national missile silos to private defense contractors
questions.explanation: Confidence Building Measures (CBMs) reduce suspicion, minimize the risk of miscalculation, and establish military hotlines and protocols between adversary nations.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which of the following was the foundational premise of the 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) adopted at the Rio Earth Summit?
options: A) All biological genetic plant material globally belongs exclusively to multinational pharmaceutical corporations
B) Developing nations are prohibited from practicing agriculture in tropical rainforest biomes
C) States possess sovereign rights over their biological resources, but have the responsibility to conserve biodiversity and ensure fair sharing of benefits
D) The United Nations General Assembly assumes direct ownership of all terrestrial flora and fauna
questions.explanation: The CBD affirmed sovereign national authority over biological resources while committing member states to conservation, sustainable use, and equitable benefit sharing from genetic resources.

questions.question: In the debate on economic globalisation, what is meant by the concept of 'Social Safety Nets'?
options: A) Physical barricades constructed around private export processing zones to prevent labour strikes
B) Subsidized internet fiber cables laid by multinational corporations in metropolitan cities
C) Tariffs imposed exclusively on agricultural raw materials imported from developed countries
D) Institutional mechanisms and welfare schemes set up by governments to cushion vulnerable and impoverished citizens from the shocks of market liberalisation
questions.explanation: Social safety nets are welfare interventions (food subsidies, public health, employment guarantees like MGNREGA) designed to protect disadvantaged groups hurt by free-market economic restructuring.

questions.question: In the general elections of 1996, which political party emerged as the single largest party in the Lok Sabha, leading to Atal Bihari Vajpayee forming a 13-day government?
questions.explanation: The BJP won 161 seats in May 1996 to become the single largest party; Atal Bihari Vajpayee was sworn in as Prime Minister but resigned after 13 days when he failed to secure majority support.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Which independent non-governmental organization headquartered in New York conducts worldwide research and advocacy on human rights, publishing annual World Reports?
questions.explanation: Human Rights Watch (HRW) is a premier global NGO based in New York that investigates abuses, exposes findings, and pressures governments to respect human rights.

questions.question: What was the landmark international norm endorsed by the UN World Summit in 2005 affirming that the international community has the duty to intervene when a sovereign state fails to protect its population from genocide, war crimes, and ethnic cleansing?
questions.explanation: The Responsibility to Protect (R2P) was adopted unanimously in 2005, affirming that sovereignty is a responsibility and if a state fails to protect its citizens from mass atrocities, the global community must act.

questions.question: Which former Finance Minister in Jawaharlal Nehru's cabinet resigned in 1950 over fundamental policy differences regarding the role and powers of the newly formed Planning Commission?
questions.explanation: Dr. John Matthai resigned as Finance Minister in May 1950, objecting to the Planning Commission functioning as a 'super-cabinet' that undermined the statutory authority of the Finance Ministry.

questions.question: Under which constitutional amendment and year was the linguistic state of Nagaland formally inaugurated as the 16th state of the Indian Union?
questions.explanation: The 13th Amendment inserted Article 371A granting special autonomy for Naga religious practices and customary laws, and the state of Nagaland was formally inaugurated on 1 December 1963.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the 'Sarvodaya Plan' drafted by Jayaprakash Narayan in January 1950?
options: A) It was a carbon-copy of the Soviet Gosplan heavy-industry model advocating state ownership of all natural resources
B) It drew inspiration from Gandhian principles and the ideas of Vinoba Bhave, advocating decentralized village self-sufficiency, small-scale agro-industries, and the ban on foreign capital
C) It was drawn up by Western Wall Street bankers urging unregulated foreign investment in mining
D) It demanded the total abolition of all rural agricultural cooperatives in favor of corporate farming
questions.explanation: Drafted by JP in 1950, the Sarvodaya Plan emphasized decentralized planning, small agriculture and cottage industries, and minimal state centralization, drawing on Gandhian socialism.

questions.question: In the aftermath of the 1962 border war with China, which famous all-party no-confidence motion—the first ever in Indian parliamentary history—was moved against the Nehru government in August 1963?
options: A) Moved by Ram Manohar Lohia
B) Moved by Shyama Prasad Mukherjee
C) Moved by Acharya J.B. Kripalani
questions.explanation: Acharya J.B. Kripalani moved the first ever No-Confidence Motion against the Nehru government in August 1963; though defeated (62 in favor, 347 against), it marked severe parliamentary interrogation of Nehru's foreign policy.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Which high-level parliamentary committee appointed in 1967 under Home Minister Y.B. Chavan investigated the epidemic of political party defections ('Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram') and recommended legislative disqualifications?
questions.explanation: The Chavan Committee on Defections submitted its report in 1968, recommending that defectors should be barred from ministerial office, laying the conceptual groundwork for the 1985 Anti-Defection Law.

questions.question: What was the significance of the 38th Constitutional Amendment Act passed during the Emergency in 1975?
options: A) It declared that the President's satisfaction in proclaiming an emergency under Article 352 was final, conclusive, and non-justiciable in any court of law
B) It abolished the Supreme Court of India and established a People's Revolutionary Tribunal
C) It nationalised all regional language daily newspapers across India
D) It declared India a one-party state under the Indian National Congress
questions.explanation: The 38th Amendment barred courts from reviewing the subjective satisfaction of the President in proclaiming an emergency; this blanket immunity was subsequently repealed by the 44th Amendment in 1978.

questions.question: Which high-ranking Punjab Police officer was shot dead by Sikh extremists on the steps of the Golden Temple in Amritsar in April 1983, marking a dangerous escalation in the Punjab crisis?
questions.explanation: Deputy Inspector General of Police A.S. Atwal was murdered in broad daylight as he stepped out of the Golden Temple after offering prayers on 25 April 1983, illustrating the breakdown of state authority.

questions.question: What was the core legal holding of the Supreme Court in the landmark S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) case concerning the federal balance?
options: A) The Union Government can dismiss any state government at its sole discretion without legislative floor tests
B) The President has absolute immunity from judicial review under all provisions of the Constitution
C) The proclamation of President's Rule under Article 356 is subject to judicial review, and the secular character of the state is a basic feature of the Constitution
D) States possess the constitutional right to secede unilaterally from the Indian Union
questions.explanation: In Bommai (1994), following the dismissal of BJP state ministries post-Babri demolition, the Supreme Court ruled that Article 356 is subject to judicial review, floor tests are mandatory, and secularism is part of the basic structure.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which Soviet republic was the first to officially declare its sovereignty in March 1990, triggering the unraveling of the Soviet Union from the Baltic periphery?
questions.explanation: Lithuania's Supreme Council, led by Vytautas Landsbergis, declared the restoration of Lithuanian independence on 11 March 1990, defying Moscow's economic blockade and troops.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which clause of the Maastricht Treaty granted Denmark and the United Kingdom official 'opt-outs' from adopting the single European currency, the Euro?
options: A) Protocols on Opt-Outs annexed to the Treaty on European Union
D) The Nice Charter of Fundamental Freedoms
questions.explanation: During negotiations for the Maastricht Treaty (1992), the UK and Denmark secured formal opt-out protocols exempting them from the obligation to join the European single currency.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which 12-point agreement signed in New Delhi in November 2005 paved the way for the end of the civil war in Nepal and the peaceful restoration of parliamentary democracy?
options: A) The Kathmandu Peace Treaty mediated by the United Nations
B) The 12-Point Understanding between the Seven Party Alliance (SPA) and the CPN (Maoist)
C) The Pokhara Accord signed by King Gyanendra and Madhav Kumar Nepal
D) The Janakpur Concordat on Federal Autonomy
questions.explanation: The 12-point understanding forged in Delhi in November 2005 united the parliamentary Seven Party Alliance and the underground Maoists against King Gyanendra's autocratic royal regime.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Under the UN Charter, which article empowers the Security Council to take military action by air, sea, or land forces as may be necessary to maintain or restore international peace and security?
questions.explanation: Chapter VII, Article 42 gives the UNSC the authority to take military action when peaceful measures under Article 41 (sanctions, embargoes) prove inadequate to preserve peace.

questions.question: Which two bilateral strategic arms reduction agreements signed between the US and the USSR/Russia in 1991 and 1993 mandated the deep, verified reduction of strategic nuclear delivery vehicles and warheads?
options: A) SALT I and SALT II
B) ABM Treaty and INF Treaty
C) Open Skies Treaty and CTBT
D) START I and START II
questions.explanation: Strategic Arms Reduction Talks (START I in 1991, START II in 1993) marked the first treaties to mandate actual reductions and dismantling of deployed strategic nuclear arsenals.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the core legal obligation imposed by the 1987 Montreal Protocol on participating nations?
options: A) A mandatory, timetable-driven phase-out of the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances, notably chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and halons
B) A binding global tax on petroleum extraction to finance deep-sea coral reef restoration
C) The immediate ban on nuclear power plants in all coastal provinces globally
D) The compulsory reallocation of all agricultural arable land to organic biodiversity sanctuaries
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol mandated specific phase-out schedules for CFCs, halons, and other ozone-depleting chemicals, accompanied by financial and technical assistance for developing nations.

questions.question: In the context of intellectual property disputes under the WTO's TRIPS agreement, which traditional Indian biological product was successfully defended by Indian scientists against a biopiracy patent granted to a US university in the 1990s?
options: A) Basmati rice exports to the European Union
B) Alphonso mango cultivars in Maharashtra
C) Turmeric (Curcuma longa) for wound healing
D) Darjeeling tea packaging trademark in Japan
questions.explanation: In 1997, India's CSIR successfully overturned a US patent granted to the University of Mississippi on the wound-healing properties of turmeric, demonstrating prior art from ancient Ayurvedic texts.
